title: All Out: Comedy About Ambition on Broadway #alloutbroadway #lawrencet...
transcript: Come with me to see Lawrence on Broadway — I mean, All Out: Comedy About Ambition. This is a companion piece to last season's All In: Comedy About Love, again featuring a rotating cast of comedians performing stories by Simon Rich. This week stars Eric Andre, Ike Barinholtz, Abbi Jacobson, and Jon Stewart. Admittedly, I am not very familiar with the work of any of these people, but I am familiar with Lawrence who performs some of their original music and provides underscoring for much of the show. This is similar to All In, but I felt they elevated the concept a bit more this time around. There appears to be a higher production value, more music, and the stories are more cohesively selected. In fact, the entire production feels more thematically focused, from the material, to the office-like set, and the specific songs that Lawrence performs. While “ambition” is a little more specific than “love” as a theme, the stories are still pretty varied, with topics ranging from astronauts, to Paul Revere's horse, to New York City transplants. I honestly didn't find the material as funny as what was featured in All In, but it was still good fun. And I was mostly there to see Lawrence anyway — they were literally on my Spotify wrapped and they did not disappoint. Given the nature of this show, this is probably not something I'd pay big bucks for, but it was certainly worth braving the cold for. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Creator found the production elevated over its predecessor with higher production value and thematic focus, but admits the material wasn't as funny and wouldn't pay premium prices — a lukewarm recommendation driven mostly by their fandom for Lawrence.
